Just to clear up the confusion, there is not a "new" IK for desktop users. We stripped out the old IK on purpose, as we said, to avoid the mouse look thrusting that people were exploiting (or sometimes unaware of). There is no IK now. It is not a new method that can be reviewed, it simply does not exist. That said, you have some interesting ideas for adding expression to mouse users, that we can consider.
(hackspanner)
I believe presence is a very important philosophy of VRChat. Good post!

@{58c6da4c23f8d63e1401d385|full_name}: when I was a desktop user I was completely unaware of it because you can't see it in the mirror because your view is moving too much to see it. I used that to nod and shake my head side to side to say no. Without these though I probably wouldn't own vr and wouldn't be here today. It gave me a slight in with the vr users enough to make friends and encourage me to get vr. My only problem with desktop mode experience was that I had no way to say I was confused, other then that I actually felt very included with everyone else. I really do hope you tackle the desktop ik soon because I know they are going to feel completely left out now

@{58c6da4c23f8d63e1401d385|full_name}: Hi Hackspanner, thanks for your input on this. If I know anyone who takes presence extremely seriously, it's you.
It's new information to me to know that the IK was actually removed so thanks for the full report.
Presence is a huge part of VRchat, maybe its standing pillar over other VR communication platforms. The removal of a not-small populations' IK is a major immersion breaker and takes the VR user out of the experience. Saying that, most KB&M users aren't bad people and we welcome them with open arms. Please keep presence a top priority at VRChat just as it has been in the past.
Thank you for all that you do.
Good Post! yes present is most importent overall and sync betwen people.

details:
TL;DR on the bottom but take the time to read.

A couple DISCLAIMERS before I begin: My mission here isn't to humiliate or degrade the designer of the IK for Mouse movements or devs in general who are working on this. I and many others understand that the IK systems are under constant redevelopment, but the point of early access is feedback, so please take it critically, but not personally. The development team does a lot of great work and we all want the game to be better and not worse in the end. I consider IK that is not working as intended a bug and not a patch, thus posted in Bug Reports.

PRESENCE:
Quick background. VRChat's goal appears to be something that no other chat community in the VR zone has right now: A high level of fidelity and presence. The graphics are good, the interactions and body movements have a level of believability which leads to a high degree of presence and the game gives you customizability without usually dipping into the strange Uncanny Valley. *This changed as of this patch*.

VRChat took a step backwards in terms of presence with this patch's review of Mouse IK solutions. As long as this is still under heavy review and work, backwards doesn't necessarily mean a lack of progress. But let's talk about where the IK has moved backwards so we can make more progress.

IK:
Idle Pose
Let's begin with what people see first, and probably one of the worst parts of the IK right now: the idle pose. This has changed from something loose and smooth, like how a body should be, to stiff and not unlike a beefcake bro on the beach. The female model idles like a male with a stick up its ass, to put it as basic as possible. The shoulders need to be relaxed, the pose needs to change, the neck needs to exist a bit more as it looks like a turtle. From the collection of female avatars I've seen in mouse mode, the idle IK in general needs to take a chill pill.

Motion
Walking and running are two things that, if done poorly, pull people observing the motion out of the game. A walk and a run need to look natural and gender-specific. The IK for mouse users fails in this regard. There is nothing feminine about the female walk and run animation. There needs to be more hip motion, shoulder motion, elbow motion. There needs to be a more light, smooth feel of motion and not a stomping run. The avatar should appear like it's easily moving under its own power, not Weird Al in his "Fat" music video.

Let's focus on specific body parts.

Head
We understand that the head is bugged and there's no IK on it. It will be fixed. The question is "how" and let's take a look at that. 

In the pre-patch IK, when a user shot their head upwards and downwards, the back bone, hips and legs all adjusted in a forward or backward arc which, when done in rapid succession, was obviously a pelvic thrust. VRChat employees are quoted as to saying it looks like "humping" and is not acceptable. The community agrees in general that it's in bad taste and oh exploitable, so let's review. Obviously one mission in this IK review is to normalize and eliminate this thrust. There are many solutions to this issue, but I like tackling these with the KISS principle (Keep It Simple, Stupid). One could remove the arcing of the body by setting the head not to arc until a certain degree threshold, utilizing the neck and head as a normal body would. Say you look 50 degrees upwards, the back doesn't have to arch, but if you look straight up, it would look unnatural if it didn't. But then we're back to the humping, right? Not at all, if we introduce the lovely concept of -delays-. If a player looks straight up, the characters head and neck goes to the 50 degree threshold and -waits a second or two- before adjusting its body to accommodate for the fact that it needs to look straight up for the user. To the user it looks like it's straight up the whole time, but to other players it looks up, waits, then looks straight up. So now, if someone decides to spaz up and down with their mouse, the character only looks up and down, not forcing its body into a convulsion of hip thrusts. The user could look up, wait two seconds, look down, wait two seconds, but instead of looking like humping, it looks like someone just being stupid, which you can't bug fix for.

Chest, Torso, Shoulders
The chest and torso appear static and they need animations and movements. The shoulders look and move like they're built for a football player, not a normal person which I discussed under Motion. They look completely unnatural and I can't review it beyond that. It's a huge presence hit for users around the user.

Feet
The feet IK wasn't worked on in the idle pose. The feet don't do anything, even when the character spins. In the old IK, the feet would adjust and replant themselves according to the characters movement. Now they're static, not unlike a spinning top, which looks absolutely ridiculous and reminds the players observing that this is a game and the presence is lost. Revert this section of the IK back to the old version as there wasn't anything wrong with the feet and leg IK for the keyboard and mouse players.

TL;DR: Focus on the head and feet section, especially how the neck connects to the body, the points about back and hip arcing, and the delays to solve the issue of "humping". Solve the losses to presence reviewed above.

I welcome any questions or comments on this write-up and everyone should expect edits to this post after the Q&A.
title: Review of New Mouse IK and Presence for VR Users
